name: Noxus AI Workers
operator: Noxus (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Noxus's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Configurable agents that use flows, integration actions, knowledge bases, tables, MCP servers, code execution and a sandbox to carry out tasks, deployed through the web app, API, SDK, chat widget, Slack, Teams, Google Chat, WhatsApp or Telegram.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

I03.n: Agents and flows are configured in a visual builder and connect to the organisation's own systems and data.
I03.span: Build sophisticated automations without writing code.

I04.n: With the Code Execution tool turned on, the agent writes and runs code.
I04.span: The agent writes and executes code

I08.n: Agents use tools and run flows to take actions themselves.
I08.span: take autonomous actions to accomplish goals

I10.n: Integrations cover several suites, including Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and Atlassian.

I11.n: An agent can be bound to external MCP servers and call their tools.
I11.span: Let the agent use tools from external MCP servers

I17.n: At CUF the AI Worker processes patient messages and routes complex cases to staff.
I17.span: Complex cases are flagged and routed to human staff instantly

I18.n: With the Human in the Loop tool, the agent acts on its own and asks a person before critical actions.
I18.span: Use HITL as a safety net for high-stakes decisions.

I20.n: The company states the agents' purpose: handling complaints, documents and tickets.
I20.span: where AI Co-workers handle complaints, documents, and tickets end-to-end

I21.n: The builder selects which actions and flows each agent may call.
I21.span: Select which actions the agent can call

I22.n: The tools page documents limits, such as web research being less reliable than knowledge bases.
I22.span: Web research is slower and less reliable than knowledge bases.

I23.n: Each agent's tools are an enumerated list chosen by the builder: the flows, actions, knowledge bases, database connections and MCP servers it may use.
I23.span: Select which flows the agent can access

I25.n: Each agent reaches only the flows, actions, knowledge bases and database connections selected for it; its SQL is generated read-only, and tables are read-only unless edits are allowed.
I25.span: Select which database connection(s) the agent may query

I26.n: A Google Chat deployment can run under a service account bot identity separate from any person.
I26.span: dedicated bot identity (separate from any human user)

I38.n: The Human in the Loop tool and Require Approval make the agent ask a person before actions run.

I39.n: An agent's deployment on a channel can be deactivated through the API.

I41.n: Logs record agent interactions including tool calls and reasoning steps, with run-level logs per run.
I41.span: Conversation metadata, tool calls, and model reasoning steps.

I45.n: When the sandbox is on, a Syd sandbox outside the agent blocks internal network ranges and requires the sandboxes:run permission.
I45.span: Private/internal network ranges are blocked; the sandbox can't reach internal services.

I47.n: Instructions written in prose set allowed behaviour and restrict access.
I47.span: Define system guidance and allowed behaviors to steer responses and restrict access

I54.n: A public status page posts incidents and offers incident update subscriptions.
I54.span: Get incident updates and maintenance status messages in Slack.

I57.n: With a Phoenix or Langfuse provider connected, users can rate agent responses up or down.
I57.span: users can submit thumbs-up / thumbs-down feedback on agent responses

I58.n: Agents read from the organisation's knowledge bases, tables and connected databases.
I58.span: Search and retrieve information from knowledge bases

I61.n: The model providers and model families an agent can use are listed.

S1.n: A named customer, CUF, reports patient communications processed by the AI Worker each month.
S1.span: patient communications processed automatically per month

S3.n: An OpenAPI 3.1.0 description of the backend API resolves; the docs llms.txt also resolves.

S4.n: A hosted MCP server lets external clients and agents call Noxus agents, conversations and workflows as tools.
S4.span: Drive the Noxus platform from any MCP-compatible client
